transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

I can’t confirm ER03’s exact meaning for this AEG hob from the code alone, so I would not treat it as a definite component fault. Given that it began immediately after pasta boiled over, the most likely cause is moisture or starchy residue affecting the touch-control area. The hob may beep and switch itself off as a protective response. 1. Switch the hob off at its isolator/fused spur and leave it isolated. Do not keep trying to use or reset it while it is beeping.
2. Once cool, wipe the entire glass—especially the control strip—using a barely damp cloth, then dry it thoroughly with a clean dry cloth. Remove any pan, cloth or utensil from the control area.
3. Leave it isolated long enough for any moisture around the controls to dry out; overnight is sensible after a substantial boil-over. Do not pour cleaner or water around the control area.
4. Restore power and test briefly with the glass fully dry. If the warning has gone, it was most likely surface moisture/residue. If Er03 returns straight away after a proper dry-out, liquid may have reached the touch-control electronics, or there may be a control-board fault. That needs a hob engineer rather than dismantling it yourself, as induction hobs contain hazardous high-voltage electronics even when switched off. If there is any burning smell, crackling, scorching, or the electrics trip, keep it isolated and arrange repair without further testing.
Ok, I wiped it dry, moved a wooden spoon that was resting on the edge, and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes. It works again now, all four zones fine. Is that all it needed?

Yes—if it is now operating normally on all four zones, that was very likely all it needed. Keep the control strip clean and fully dry, and avoid resting utensils, pan handles or cloths over it. If ER03 returns when the glass is clean, dry and clear, especially without another spill, leave it switched off at the isolator and arrange an engineer, as that could indicate moisture beneath the glass or a touch-control fault.

candidates: Moisture or food residue activating the touch-control area after the boil-over (high)
Liquid ingress beneath the glass affecting the touch-control electronics (medium)
Control electronics fault unrelated to the spill (low)

reading.symptom: Keeps beeping, shows Er03, then switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "Keeps beeping, shows Er03, then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Moisture/residue or an object activating the touch controls after the boil-over (high)

reading.symptom: previous beeping/error has cleared; hob works again

plan: They asked: "Is that all it needed?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: Wiped the hob dry: It works again
Moved a wooden spoon resting on the edge: It works again
